newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB adds aggressively, money rates ease.
newsitem.headline: SNB adds aggressively, money rates ease.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) added liquidity to the domestic money market in early trade at the usual time for its routine activities in an aggressive operation which traders said showed it was looking for lower short-term rates.

The SNB did not provide details of its operations, but did confirm that it was remaining generous after it said Wednesday it would add significant liquidity to the money market to work against the Swiss franc's recent rise.
"We are fairly active... continuing the generous supply of liquidity to the market that we described yesterday," an SNB spokesman said in response to an enquiry.
The SNB does not make public the rates on its money market operations, and does not formally target short-term rates.
One trader said that the SNB was in the market around 0700 GMT adding via swaps. The SNB was said to have added at 150 pips, which was seen as aggressive, the trader said.

A second trader said it appeared the SNB had "clearly eased" by roughly a quarter percentage point, and was aiming for a level of 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 percent for money rates. Rates recently have tended to trade above 1-1/2.
Traders also said the SNB also added liquidity at 1-3/8 percent for five days, a rate below the 1-5/8 percent seen in recent weeks.
Tomorrow/next money was also quoted lower after the operations at 1-3/8 to 1-1/2 percent, traders said.
Currency traders said the market was nervous before the SNB's regular weekly policy meeting, amidst expectations in some quarters that it could cut its discount rate, now at 1.00 percent.
The level matches the historic low seen in 1978/79.
But money market traders at large Swiss banks generally did not expect the SNB to cut its discount rate at today's meeting. The results of the meeting are expected at 1400 GMT.
